ground_truth.description: The inspect.markcoroutinefunction(self) marking is unnecessary. AsyncMock awaits any side_effect return value for which asyncio.iscoroutine() is true, and __call__ is async def so it always returns a coroutine; the marker changes no behavior on any Python version (as the inline comment itself notes). It adds complexity without functional effect.

_UuidDispatcher (an instance with async __call__) is passed as AsyncMock side_effect; AsyncMock awaits a side_effect only when iscoroutinefunction(effect) is true, which for an instance holds only after inspect.markcoroutinefunction (3.12+). On Python 3.11, which fused-memory declares supported (requires-python >=3.11, pyright pythonVersion 3.11), the guard is skipped and AsyncMock returns an un-awaited coroutine, so every converted call site (test_force_rebuilds_all, test_partial_failure_continues, the TestMemoryServiceRebuildEntitySummaries service fixture) hands production a coroutine (rebuild_entity_summaries raises TypeError on non-dict results) and assert_all_dispatched fails. The inline comment claiming AsyncMock 'checks asyncio.iscoroutine(result)' on 3.11 is false. The replaced async-def closure worked on every version.

test_works_without_markcoroutinefunction claims to prove _UuidDispatcher works on Python 3.11 (markcoroutinefunction absent), but it awaits dispatch(...) directly and never routes through AsyncMock(side_effect=dispatch), the only path where the marker matters. It passes in exactly the configuration where real usage returns an un-awaited coroutine, so it cannot detect the 3.11 breakage it names.

test_delegates_to_backend reaches the dispatcher via service.graphiti.rebuild_entity_from_edges.side_effect.assert_all_dispatched() because the service fixture builds the dispatcher without exposing it; the call is untyped (mock attribute) and couples the test to the fixture's wiring, and the other tests sharing the fixture never check dispatch completeness.

_UuidDispatcher.dispatched duplicates the call record AsyncMock already keeps (await_args_list), so completeness could be asserted statelessly from the mock. The task explicitly requested a tracking set plus assert_all_dispatched, so the redundancy is task-mandated and minor; the residual cost is the stateful class that this choice motivated.

_uuid_dispatch became a one-line pass-through to the _UuidDispatcher constructor, and the class and factory carry near-identical multi-paragraph docstrings (value types, unexpected-uuid behaviour, tracking API): two names and two copies of one contract that can drift (and already contain the false 3.11 and 'surfaces immediately' claims). A closure or a single entity with one short docstring would suffice; the mapping is also typed as bare dict.

test_dispatch_docstring_documents_exception_support only asserts the two docstrings are non-empty; its name claims it checks that exception support is documented. It pins prose existence, guards no behaviour, and its own docstring concedes the behavioural tests already cover the feature.

The AST cross-reference guard in test_partial_failure_continues_still_raises_runtime_error_not_value_error was loosened from 'RuntimeError appears in a raise' to 'RuntimeError appears as any bare-name Call'; the set is still named error_names but now collects every called name (_uuid_dispatch, AsyncMock, StaleSummaryResult, ...), and any stray RuntimeError(...) anywhere in the test body would satisfy it, so it no longer shows RuntimeError reaches the dispatcher or is raised.

The test module, already past 2,600 lines, grows by ~155 lines of generic mock-dispatch infrastructure plus its own unit-test class (TestUuidDispatch), none specific to rebuild_entity_summaries; the helper and its self-tests would sit better in conftest.py or a small test-helper module.

assert_all_dispatched checks only for mapped uuids that were never called, not for unexpected uuids, although dispatched records them. The docstrings say an unexpected uuid 'surfaces immediately', but MemoryService.rebuild_entity_summaries runs asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) and accumulates the AssertionError as an errors entry, so a test that does not inspect errors (e.g. test_delegates_to_backend) would pass with extra dispatches.
The TestUuidDispatch tests rebuild the same Alice/Bob result-dict mapping literals and dispatch-call boilerplate in each test instead of sharing a constant or builder.

The mapping parameter is typed as bare dict although its contract is Mapping[str, dict | BaseException]; re-raising the same exception instance on repeated dispatch of a uuid accumulates traceback frames, a minor hazard for error-detail assertions.

task.title: Enhance _uuid_dispatch with dispatch tracking and exception support
task.description:
Two related improvements to the `_uuid_dispatch` helper in `fused-memory/tests/test_rebuild_entity_summaries.py`:

1. **Dispatch tracking** — `_uuid_dispatch` currently doesn't verify that all mapped UUIDs were actually dispatched. If production code silently skips an entity, the mock won't catch it (tests rely on downstream aggregate assertions like `rebuilt == 2`). Add a tracking set inside `_side_effect` and expose an `assert_all_dispatched()` method or return the tracking set so callers can verify `len(called) == len(mapping)` after the test action.

2. **Exception support + unify _fail_uuid1** — `_fail_uuid1` (around line 826) duplicates the dispatch-by-uuid pattern but adds exception support. Extend `_uuid_dispatch` to accept mapping values that are either dicts (returned directly) or exceptions (raised), then rewrite `_fail_uuid1` as `_uuid_dispatch({'uuid-1': RuntimeError('FalkorDB timeout'), 'uuid-2': {...}})`. This eliminates duplication and enforces a single dispatch convention across the module.
